briefing.opening: Hello everyone. We will now begin the climate briefing for September 24, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis and Global Impacts
sections.content: Recent extreme heatwaves in Southern Europe are causing affluent populations to migrate northward [1], and direct traces of climate change are appearing, such as a 100-year-old cathedral being submerged by the sea in Vietnam [2]. These global heatwaves are expanding threats to human health, coinciding with a situation where global warming and the reckless pursuit of fossil fuel capitalism are identified as the greatest threats to public health [21, 43]. Unprecedented changes are being detected across ecosystems, with an increase in coastal flood days [25, 34], tropical sea turtles nesting for the first time on California beaches, and a surge in migratory insects in the UK [46, 48]. This suggests that climate change, technology, and vast amounts of information are accelerating risk changes, akin to the analogy that climate change is progressing like an 'escalator' and humanity is like a 'blob' at its bottom [31, 39].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic and International Efforts for Carbon Neutrality and Renewable Energy Expansion
sections.content: The Republic of Korea is strengthening international climate cooperation efforts by agreeing on the final text of the Memorandum of Understanding for a climate agreement with Nepal [3]. Domestically, efforts for climate change adaptation and renewable energy expansion continue, including strengthening the production base for Iksan ginger in preparation for heatwaves and droughts [4], and Chuncheon City's ninth consecutive selection for the Renewable Energy Convergence Support Project [14]. Furthermore, various local governments, including Yongin City, Okcheon County, and Gwangmyeong City, are encouraging citizens to practice carbon neutrality in their daily lives through carbon neutrality point systems and recruitment for Net-Zero Energy Cafes. KORAIL's 'Local Love Rail Travel' also received the UIC Sustainable Award, recognizing its contribution to carbon neutrality [5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13]. Internationally, Germany is redesigning its power grid to suit the era of renewable energy using Artificial Intelligence (AI) [18], and Greater Manchester has moved a step closer to a carbon-neutral public transport system through its Clean Energy Agreement [45]. These efforts present practical solutions to climate change, and the economic benefits of the eco-friendly transition are also being highlighted, particularly in the UK, where driving an electric vehicle can be up to nine times cheaper than a fossil fuel vehicle [42, 49].

sections.title: ⚠️ Challenges and Policy Dilemmas in Energy Transition
sections.content: Globally, 1700 GW of renewable energy projects are awaiting grid connection due to insufficient power grids, and the International Energy Agency (IEA) has warned of the urgent need for grid modernization [19]. Domestically, active discussions on energy transition policies are underway, including public hearings on reforming the renewable energy contract market [15], parliamentary audits verifying an energy blueprint encompassing everything from mega-project power grids to renewable energy and nuclear power [16], and public development forums for renewable energy [17]. However, policy implementation faces difficulties, such as the groundbreaking climate change superfund bill being blocked once again in New York [35]. In Australia, debates over the direction of energy policy are intensifying, with the coalition government advocating for the abandonment of renewable energy plans, increased fossil fuel use, and a nuclear revival, all while promising cheaper electricity [47]. This situation, amidst climate change, technology, and vast information accelerating risk changes [31], further raises concerns about what will happen when the El Niño phenomenon meets climate change [32].

sections.title: 🌍 Research and Awareness Promotion on Climate Change
sections.content: In-depth scientific research on ecosystems is being conducted worldwide, including studies on the impact of climate change on Minnesota trees and raptors [26, 27, 30]. Efforts to raise public awareness continue, such as addressing 'frank talks about climate change' at FCAT meetings [36] and showcasing practical solutions during Climate Week NYC [42]. In London, young artists are using their talents to convey climate change messages [41], and artworks like Diane Burko's 'Extraction' vividly illustrate the reality of climate change [29]. These efforts foster discussions on the interconnectedness of climate change, knowledge, inspiring the next generation, and water [44], emphasizing the need to listen to the voices of at least its victims, especially poor nations, who will suffer the most from climate change, if not to climate change science itself [37, 38]. Meanwhile, some non-profit organizations are presenting new perspectives on threats alongside climate change, asserting that Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the fastest threat, surpassing climate change and inequality, and urging the UN to adopt an 18th global goal [28, 40].

briefing.closing: It is crucial to comprehensively understand the severity of the climate crisis discussed in today's briefing, along with the various efforts to overcome it, and the policy challenges that still remain. This concludes today's climate briefing.
